about: The map and its places: the areas, their size and shape, the beach, glades, paths, walls, scenery pieces, set pieces, the treehouse, home and the legends' clearings and relics.

map.what: The forest's size: how many areas there are and how big each one is.
map.notes: The forest: mapAreas x mapAreas areas cut by the fractal partition. An area is areaSize x areaScale metres across on average (areaScale 4 makes them four times as wide as the first 28 m areas; push it for bigger).

decisions.quote: The map as a whole should be circular rather than square, with a buffer zone with no runestones around the edge

map.islandAreas.what: How many areas the island has round home, and its round, buffered shape.

decisions.rest: the journey's islands: 10, the home island for now; ?island=10|20|...|64|home, ?island=off for the radius map
5.6: about 96; for about 100 areas: the best bots wake about 20 in a run, and half the creatures and trees run faster; 7.9 gave about 196, as many as the old 14 x 14
the land map, rules/land.ts: round the borders of the playable areas, the ring of areas round them and, where it's near, the ring past that

map.islandAreas.notes: the island is home and exactly this many more areas, those nearest home's, round, its radius halfway out to the next (0: the radius below). shape circle: the playable areas are those whose centres lie within radius areas of home's [2], and only they get runestones, soundsystems, legends, relics and creatures and wake in waves; past them a buffer ring buffer areas deep (1 to 1.5), forest she can fly over where nothing happens; her flight's edge is the island's coast [3], soft over its last push metres (her speed outward easing to nothing at the edge, and a drift of up to drift m/s taking her back in); the forest goes on edge areas past it, into the fog.

map.island.what: Which island is played: home, built from the kinds she knows, or another by its roster.
map.island.notes: "home" plays home by roster, one area per kind she knows (the 10 kinds introduced at home and each kind whose island she's found, map.found: growing outward, its first areas the same; islandAreas its least, the kinds again past one each), its legends dealt each night, 1 in 5 areas; a kind's name (?island=fox) plays that kind's island, its own seed (where it lies on the sea chart) and size by phase (10 a phase), its roster that kind plentiful, 1-3 kinds new to its phase and the rest by bearing; empty, areas of random types as before.

map.found.what: the kinds whose islands she's found (the night's legends favour the others).

map.phase.what: How an island grows out from home, its outline rounder or more lobed, bayed and armed the further out it is.
map.phase.notes: an island grows out from home over its areas' neighbours, each step the area nearest home for the island's reach that way, by its phase's shape (shapes[phase], index 0 home: near-round; 1 gently lobed; 2 bays and a peninsula; 3 arms and inlets; 4 and 5 strongly irregular): lobes, how far its outline swells and shrinks round home (a share of its reach) over harmonics bumps; arms, how far its peninsulas reach past it (a share), armCount[0] to [1] of them, each armWidth radians across; bays, how deep its bays cut in, bayCount[0] to [1] of them; jitter, each area's own seeded nudge in areas (ragged edges). Home's neighbours are always its first. an island's phase when it isn't one by roster (?phase=0 to 5; a kind's island takes its own).

map.coast.what: How irregular the island's coastline is, with gentle bays and headlands rather than a perfect circle.

decisions.quote: The island shouldn't be a totally perfect circle; make the coast slightly irregular

map.coast.notes: which areas are playable and which the buffer's goes by their centres' distance from home over the same seeded coast, up to amp of its radius in or out (0 for a perfect circle): harmonics gentle bays and headlands (from two round the island up), plus detail (a share) of finer wobble. shape square: mapAreas x mapAreas as before (?shape=square to compare). ?mapAreas=<n> on the circular map sets the radius for about n x n areas.

biomeLooks.what: How strongly an island's forests take on its biome's look, more so the further out its ring.

decisions.quote: Lower phase non-home biome areas can be semi-temperate looking; higher phase biomes are more extreme; so there's a smoother transition between phases

biomeLooks.notes: How strongly an island's forests take its biome's look (art/flora/biomes.js), by its ring [1]: strength[0] for phase from's islands, strength[1] the next ring out, and so on, the last for any further; each mixes the biome's look toward temperate's by 1 - strength (1 the full look). Rings nearer in are temperate. Its own art: a ring's strength is in its key (rules/lakeLooks.ts biomeKey).

lakes.what: Lakes on the outer islands: some areas are water she can fly over but not land on, some with biome looks like frozen or lava lakes.

decisions.rest: render/lakeLooks.ts, each lake the sea chart's look for it

lakes.notes: Lakes [1]: from phase 1 some of an island's areas are water, map.shapes[phase].lakes (fewest, most) of them, each lakeSize (fewest, most) areas, never home or its neighbours, the rest of the island still joined (rules/islandGrowth.ts placeLakes); no beaches but a small shore, their water lighter than the sea; she flies over them in the treetops but never lands on the water, and on foot she and every creature stop at the shore. The biome lakes in play [2]: the north's glacier's peaks kept glacierClear metres under her treetop flight (treetopHeight), and the hot springs' (the rust pools') steam: on, puffs rising rise metres over life seconds, size metres across, at opacity, a vent every spacing metres over their deep water.

lakes.shore.what: metres of bare shore round the water (no trees, nothing placed).

lakes.pad.what: how far from the water anything on foot stops.

lakes.koi.what: the share of lakes with koi in them (DECISION FOR ED).

lakes.biomeFrom.what: the island phase from which its lakes take the look of its compass biomes on the sea chart (frozen, lava, oasis, sinkhole, glacial tarn, tar pit, rust pool, lily pond; app/chartOutlines.worker.ts), before it plain water [1].

decisions.quote: biome lakes can start appearing one phase earlier
decisions.rest: 3, it was 4, the first uncharted islands

lakes.biomeFirstShare.what: the share of that first phase's lakes that take them, each lake seeded, the rest plain water; further out all of them, further in none [1].

decisions.quote: half the lakes in the third ring are special. Further out they're all special, further in they're all plain

chart.what: The sea chart (the map table and chart.html; render/chart/seaChart.ts, render/chart/moon.ts).

chart.moon.what: The moon rising and circling over the sea chart each time it opens.

decisions.quote: islands casting shadows from the moon orbiting the map screen
have the moon rise over the North West edge of the map as you open the map screen

chart.moon.notes: each time the chart opens the moon rises over its edge at bearing from (degrees, 0 north, clockwise: -45 the north-west) over rise seconds, from just under the horizon to height degrees, then goes round once every turn seconds; every island's relief throws a shadow away from it, across the sea and into its own valleys, shadow its darkest (0 none, 1 black), the hills' shading following it.

chart.moon.disc.what: its disc drawn in the sky past the rim at its bearing (hidden behind the world).

chart.edgeBand.what: (#746: "add empty sea around the edge of the map"): the empty sea past the furthest islands, the disc's radius beyond theirs as a share of it (0 as before; at most 0.6).

chart.sailHold.what: How long the use button is held on an island at the sea chart to sail there.

decisions.quote: You have to hold the button to select a new island to sail to (ring fills)

chart.sailHold.notes: Seconds the use button (E, Enter, the pad's square) or the mouse is held on an island at the map table's chart to sail there, its ring filling [1]; let go early, nothing. A click only chooses.

islands.what: How the other islands look on the sea chart and in the dream bubbles: their coastlines and shapes.
islands.notes: Islands other than home (the wave 2 finale's dream bubbles and the sea chart; rules/islandShape.ts, art/islands.js; Ed, docs/backlog/journey.md): coast, the coastline's knobs as map.coast's (amp, the most it strays from round, a share of the radius; harmonics, how many bays and headlands; detail, the finer wobble), stronger than home's so every island has a shape of its own, read at a bubble's 30 pixels.

beach.what: The strip of sand round the island's edge, where she can lie down to stargaze and meet other witches.

decisions.quote: Outside of the circular map, there is the sea. A beach surrounds the island, and the calm dark water reflects the sky. You can hear the sound of the waves. If you try and fly past the beach, you land and stargaze (the party lying down pose). Other witches can be found on the beach occasionally; if you land near them, you chat, hold hands, and hug. Try and do this in a way that doesn't cost performance - most games won't ever go to the beach, it's just an Easter egg for adventurers.

move the camera further and lower to show off the moon reflecting on the water and the beach and the sky ... check in 12 different directions for a nice composition and smoothly interpolate between them
the bend shader applies so that you can see the sky
it's stronger than usual, so the sky takes up more of the screen
If you land near another witch, and you stargaze together, and you wait a few seconds, little hearts will start appearing near you both, floating upwards and disappearing
they last longer and disappear more slowly (5 seconds)
I think there should always be beach witches, but there are only a handful spread around it
Beach witches appear solo

beach.notes: The beach [1]: sand over the last width metres inside her flight's edge (nothing grows or stands on it), the sea from shore metres past the edge, the hills eased over ease metres down to sand metres high where the sand starts and to sea metres at the water. Flying on out over the sand for restAfter seconds she lands (from the treetops too) and lies down to stargaze; any other way gets her up. Lying there facing out to sea (the north coast: the camera always looks north), the bend keeps only camera.seaward of itself, so the open water isn't dropped below a horizon of sand. Lying down, the camera stands by her bearing round the coast [2]: camera.bearings, twelve entries every 30 degrees from the north, clockwise: angle (degrees below the horizon), distance (metres back), look (metres over her it aims at), side (metres east it stands and aims: out over the water on the east and west coasts, so the shore runs up the picture with the sea beside it) and bend (the share of the stargazing bend kept there: none facing the open sea to the north, so the water isn't dropped below a horizon of sand; camera.seaward does the same on the way down to the water), joined smoothly all the way round. Lying there [3] the world bends stargazeCurve times the treetops' curve [4], eased in and out over about gazeEase seconds, so the night sky opens up over the sea. Lying there with a beach witch [5]: after hearts.after seconds a ❤️ rises off one or the other every hearts.every[0] to [1] seconds, for hearts.life seconds each, until either gets up; the two stay lying together until she moves. A 💌 come down on the sand or the sea [6] rests letterLinger seconds, fading over the last letterFade, bobbing gently on the water. witchChance of runs [7] have spots[0] to spots[1] spots spread round the coast (evenly, each nudged by up to a third of the gap), each with witches[0] to witches[1] witches [8]; landing within meet metres of them and keeping still for idleAfter seconds, one chats, holds hands, hugs and stargazes with her, turn seconds each. None of it is drawn or heard unless she's within shown metres of the sand, nor the witches stepped beyond simRange. on false: forest to the edge, as before.

beach.grain.what: how far each of the sand's art pixels is lightened or darkened at random, 0.14 = ±7%; the sand and sea draw their art pixels doubled until each covers at least a screen pixel (render/ground.ts), so the grain stays chunky under the beach's far, low camera.

decisions.quote: The beach is not pixelated like everything else

beach.vary.what: the sand's width round the coast, width times e to the amp times a seeded smooth noise of harmonics bays and narrows; where the noise is lowest (below -rocky, of -1 to 1) it turns rocky, narrowing to rockyWidth metres; never under min.

decisions.quote: The beach can be more irregularly shaped

beach.decor.what: Shells, starfish, seaweed, pebbles and footprint trails scattered along the beach.

decisions.quote: a few beach decorations, sparsely: shells, star fish, conch, footprints of people and creatures ... just nature

decisions.rest: too many on the beach, so finds and trails halved, to 0.35 and 0.035

beach.decor.notes: round the coast in sectors sectors, about finds finds a sector (shells, starfish, a conch, seaweed, pebbles; rocks on a rocky stretch), each sector with a trails chance of a trail of prints[0] to prints[1] footprints (bare feet, paws, hooves, a bird's, weighted by kinds) wandering along the sand and fading out [2]; all of it on the wet and dry sand, the clear metres of it nearest the woods left bare.

beach.dolphins.what: Dolphins leaping off the east coast while she's on the beach.

decisions.rest: their timetable rules/seaLife.ts, drawn by render/dolphins.ts

beach.dolphins.notes: leaping off the east coast, within arc radians of due east, one every every[0] to [1] seconds, pair of them in twos, out[0] to [1] metres past the water's edge from her and ahead[0] to [1] metres north of that (away from the camera: the stargazing bend drops anything much more than 20 m ahead of her below the screen), each leap length metres along the coast and height high over time seconds.

beach.kraken.what: A kraken's tentacles rising off the west coast now and then while she's on the beach.
beach.kraken.notes: off the west coast, within arc radians of due west, a slot every every seconds, chance of them holding a rising: tentacles[0] to [1] tentacles rising one after another out[0] to [1] metres past the water's edge from her and ahead[0] to [1] metres north of that, each over time seconds, and in head of them the dome of its head and its eye.

arena.what: Every area is kept mostly open round its centre and its soundsystem, so fights have room.
arena.notes: every area is mostly open within radius metres of its centre and its soundsystem, for fights (they range 15 to 45 m), and (Ed: softer edges; then, at v473, a smaller clearing and a long soft gradient from the area's edge to near its runestone) the woods thicken over a band band metres wide beyond it, across most of the area, along curve (linear: thinning in from right past the open middle; smooth: a slow start), lone trees and bushes thinning out into the clearing, its edge wobbled by noise (a share of the band) so it's no ring; both times fight.scale.

arena.bushes.what: the share of the undergrowth and the ground cover left in its open middle.

areaSizeVariance.what: How much areas vary in size, some small and some large.

decisions.quote: make areas larger; each is effectively a fighting arena

areaSizeVariance.notes: (0-1) makes areas vary in size, some small, some large. borderLayers sets how wiggly borders are. Ed [1]: 14 x 14 areas of 168 m (areaScale 6), about the same world as 20 x 112 m.

clearingSize.what: (0-1): how far out from an area's centre the ground stays fully open.

clearingFalloff.what: (0-1): over how much of the way to the border trees thicken to full density (small: crisp clearing edges).

gladeAmount.what: How much of the woods is open in random glades.
gladeAmount.notes: (0-1) of the woods is open in random glades about gladeScale metres across; trees sit on a staggered grid treeSpacingX by treeSpacingZ metres, so no two crowns pile up. A tree is left out where its crown (crownHalfWidth either side, crownHeight up) would hang over a clearing seen from the treetops.

areaEdgeBlend.what: Trees and bushes near an area's border take the look of the area next door, so borders blend rather than form a line.

decisions.rest: 40: #887, so the planting blends across the borders; it was 20

decisions.quote: The effect that makes tree placement from neighbouring areas blend should be increased
I don't think tree blending borders need to wander, as the area edges themselves are already noisy

areaEdgeBlend.notes: Blended area edges: each tree and bush takes its look (its area type) from a point up to width metres away [1], the offset mostly the plant's own, drawn independently of its neighbours' (stray of it: 0.85, Ed's #887 feedback, so the kinds interleave tree by tree rather than in clumps; it was 0.5), the rest a smooth noise scale metres across so the band doesn't run dead straight; the neighbour's share ramps from about half at the border to none width metres in. And the band itself wanders [2]: every plant near one spot shifted alike by up to warp metres, a noise warpScale metres across, so a border reads as ragged, gradual mixing rather than a line; width doubled to 80 then (it was 40). warp 0 since [3], kept as a knob. The pause page's Area blend slider sets width (a new map: it reloads). Only the look: creatures, partifying and the party border keep the exact borders.

areaEdgeBlend.tufts.what: How far the ground cover blends across area borders as the trees do.
areaEdgeBlend.tufts.notes: the share of the band the ground cover blends over (0: the tufts keep the exact border, as before; they lie on the area's own floor, which keeps its edge, and a cave mouth's bare ground taking a grassland's thick grass 40 m in read as wrong; 1 blends them as the trees); their cell (a legend circle's floor, an arena) stays the exact one either way.

groundBlend.what: How neighbouring areas' floor textures meet, along a meandering, blended border.
groundBlend.notes: How neighbouring areas' floor textures meet (Ed, v160): the border is warped by noise in two octaves (up to warp metres over about 40 m, and fine metres over about 6 m), so it meanders rather than following the texture's grid; across a band metres wide the two floors mix pixel by pixel, by noise and (dither) an ordered dither, like grass creeping into dirt. Visual only. ?blend=off turns it off.

ground.what: Low rises and hollows in the ground's lighting, so it doesn't look flat.
ground.notes: The ground's fake relief (Ed, v171: so the ground doesn't look flat): low rises and hollows from noise about relief.scale metres across, tilting the ground's lighting by relief.strength (0 flat) so the witch's light and the campfires pick out the bumps, and hollows shaded darker by relief.shade. ?relief=0 turns it off.

ground.layout.what: Every area's runestone stands on a rise and every legend's clearing lies in a hollow.

decisions.rest: rules/terrain.ts; relayed by the coordinator: runestones on high ground, legends in low, trees thicker low down

ground.layout.notes: every area's runestone stands on a rise and every legend clearing lies in a hollow, rise and dip times the hills' amplitude high and deep (0.15 of 40 m: 6 m), each easing out over reach metres (kept short and low: the stones are about 110 m apart, a clearing about 65 m from its stone, and the slopes must stay under the camera's sightline) (the plateaus then level each one, so a stone tops a knoll and a clearing sits in a dell); trees grow up to trees (a share) thicker in the lowest ground and thinner on the highest, by the land's height over half the hills' amplitude (most of it lies within that). Drawing and tree placement only: the rules still move on flat ground.

wisps.what: Will-o'-the-wisps drifting through the wild areas near her, none near a party.
wisps.notes: Will-o'-the-wisps in the wild areas [1]: a seeded chance per square of ground (cell m) within reach of her; none within partyNear of a partified area, the full chance from partyFar; height [low, high] m, drift m, a cycle of period s (fade in, linger, fade out, gone); core and halo size in art pixels; colour.

glades.what: The clearings where sleeping legends lie.

decisions.quote: Sleeping legends should be in a small circular clearing, where they sit near the top of the circle. This magical clearing should be lit with an eerie twilight with glowing motes rising in it.
When you go into the legend clearing, the rest of the forest should get darker. Maybe switch off the witch's glow when she's in there.

glades.notes: The sleeping legends' clearings [1]: art builder 1 places them (the map's glades); until then one round each sleeping legend, radius metres across with the legend top of the way toward its top. Only those within reach metres of the witch, the nearest 4, are lit. Inside one [2]: the forest's light and haze outside the clearing's own twilight dim by dark (0 none, 1 black), her own glow goes by glowOff (1: off; her moonlit rim stays), both eased in and out over fade seconds.

glades.hue.what: the twilight's colour (a cool violet dusk, against the party's amber).

glades.light.what: its pool, filling the circle and soft at its edge.

glades.edge.what: the ring at its edge at full (a quarter of it always marks the circle), which brightens with the witch inside it or a quest sigil or relic put down in it, easing at edgeEase a second.

glades.motes.what: per to a clearing, rising rise metres a second to height metres, size art pixels, in hue and sat at bright.

treehouse.what: The witch's home in the great oak beside the dancefloor: where it stands, its deck and rooms, how she walks and lands there, and the oak's crown, lights and warm glow over it.

decisions.quote: The treehouse should be 5m due north of the dance floor, outside the speaker ring
put the treehouse north-west of the dancefloor
decisions.rest: the oak since,:, its Terrace's open south-east rim towards it

decisions.quote: a circle with a wooden floor and a balustrade sitting on the ent. You land on it by being at treetop height, and during the night time slower 10x
The deck sits at 22 m
The table holding the decks is along the curved bottom edge of the platform
decisions.rest: decks, from where she stands behind them, inner metres out, to their front, outer, from to to degrees round, 90 due south; the Ent's art, art/ent.js, draws them there
docs/backlog/treehouse.md step 1; treehouse.house, on in place of the deck; rules/treehouse.ts

decisions.quote: she shouldn't use her broom until she steps off the balcony
walking without sitting on a broom ... is too slow
when you're inside the treehouse in an enclosed room (i.e. not the terrace) the forest behind the tree should be black
When the forest has loaded, fade it in gradually behind the whole treehouse

quote: The witch should have a canopy circle cut around her in the treehouse
Room canopy cuts should fade in rather than be instant

decisions.quote: lights at half
The spiral with 2 strands, smoothed so it sags across the gaps
warm light only

treehouse.notes: The witch's treehouse, home [1][2]: its foot (the Terrace's middle; clear metres round it) stands gap metres beyond the dancefloor's ring of speakers (so however many speakers or how far out, it stays outside them; 22 keeps the oak's rooms, up in its crown, clear of the dancefloor's clearing), at angle degrees (-135: north-west; -90 due north, straight up the screen), always facing south, to the floor and the camera; and keeps a clearing of clear metres round its foot (at least the art's footprint: 8.2 m for the v2 tower); its lantern and fairy lights light lightReach metres round at lightStrength. The game starts with her sitting on its terrace; the first move or rise takes her off. The deck [3]: on (false: the old treehouse), a round deck radius metres across its middle at the Ent (the treehouse's spot), its floor height metres up [4]; in the treetops, landing within radius + grace metres of its middle lands her on it; she walks it, kept rail metres inside its edge, round the map table in its middle (table metres round; Ed: "The world map is in the centre"; E within tableUse metres of its edge opens the sea chart) and behind the decks along its south edge [5], where she starts and comes back, seat metres south of the middle. On it, landed, time runs as in a calm legend circle (legendCircle.slow). The house [6][7]: its floor the oak's one shape (config/house/shape.js) at height metres, rail its edge's keep-in, the Terrace one of its trunk rooms at the treehouse's spot, its layout config/house/base.json's (terrace: the open rim, the decks, her seat, the magic circle): at treetop height she flies straight onto the Terrace and lands over landTime seconds, walks off its rim to fly again, or, with no broom (fall.on, a switch till the brooms are objects), falls for fall.time seconds and comes back at the magic circle (circle.out south of the hub's centre, circle.r), where a knockout brings her back too. The house's walk [8]: on foot in the house (the hub, the balcony, the rooms) she walks, walk metres a second, not at her broom's groundSpeed [9]; her walk cycle is drawn for stride metres a second, its steps quickening above it so her feet don't slide. The dark behind the house [10][11]: with dark.on, on foot in the house, any room or the Terrace, only the house, the Ent's crowns and her are drawn, over black, till the island's ready (its art drawn: g.islandReady); then the forest fades in behind the whole house over dark.reveal seconds and stays behind every room after; leaving the house before then, it comes back from where she stands over dark.fade seconds, and through the telescope it fades in over the same. The great oak's crown [12]: with crown.on, one crown over the whole house in place of the rooms' leaf roofs, grown from the house's outline (config/house/outline.json) and crown.seed: its lobes, the oak's limbs through its gaps, the Terrace's notch open to the sky out to its edge, its string lights and its far landmark. Indoors [13]: the crown cleared over her room (or branch) opens over crown.cutFade seconds as she comes in and fills back in over the same as she leaves, and the forest's hole round her (canopyCutout: its size, its soft edge) is cut in it too, round where she's drawn, opening and closing with it; the Terrace's notch stays open as ever. Its lights [14]: lights of its strings hung, whole strings by a hash (0.5; 1 every one), each string hung its own way (rules/crown.ts: swags with their own sag and steps, some part way, tails hanging off them, spirals round the big limbs, drapes near or long across a gap, garlands part way or all round, tilted and wavering, the bulbs the same spacing on every one, Ed: "The same bulb spacing"). Its wrap [15]: wrap long strands spiralling out over its top from its middle as seen from above, in place of its drapes and garlands, each resting on the lobes, its height smoothed along it and sagging across the gaps between them (rules/crown.ts makeCrown); 2, as Ed chose; 0 its drapes and garlands instead. Its warm light [16]: warm times the house's light spilling up onto the lobes' and limbs' undersides over its open rooms (render/crown.ts warmAt: a glow round each room's middle 1.5 m over its floor, its size and 3 m more across, worked out once as the crown's made), in flat quarter steps; 0 none, 1 as Ed chose it from the mock; both live on the pause page's Oak crown group.

home.what: Home's area [1]: the map is cut with home first, a circle round the dancefloor out past the treehouse's footprint (its distance and clear) and margin metres more all home's; the areas round it are cut round it, their centres kept at least gap of an area beyond the circle.

decisions.quote: Home area should be big enough that the whole circle, centre the dancefloor, edge the treehouse, is within it

scenes.what: Small vignettes and large landmarks (a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a cemetery, castle ruins) placed about the island.
scenes.notes: Scenes [1]: small vignettes (a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a picnic gone wild...) and large landmarks (a cemetery, a car park, ruined churches and temples, castle ruins...), each a few pieces counting as one, each at most once per map. An area gets one with chance, if a scene that suits it (its suits) is still unused; it stands off to the side of the area's centre, its footprint clear of the paths, gameplay and other features, trees kept off it, mirrored at random. footprint: the farthest piece's authored offset times scale, plus pad metres (a test checks it covers the art's own).

scenes.featured.what: one of ids (seeded) placed on a map at its chance, in an area it suits if there is room, else in any [1].

decisions.rest: the temple ruins on most islands,: the Greek temple or the classical ruins, and: temple-* is every seeded classical ruin scene, art/landmarks.js CLASSICAL_PLANS; an id ending in * takes every scene it starts

grounds.what: Old playgrounds and sports grounds in some areas, off to the side of their centre.
grounds.notes: Old playgrounds and sports grounds (the relics art's arrangements): an area has one with chance (not home), off to the side of its centre, keeping a clearing of radius metres (per kind) where nothing grows. Kinds [1]: only the playground; the sports grounds are left out of kinds.

legendClearing.what: Each sleeping legend lies in a small round clearing of its own, sized to fit it.
legendClearing.notes: Each area's sleeping legend lies in a small circular clearing of its own [1], where no tree or decor stands: radius metres across from its middle (species: a radius for that legend, sized to fit it: half its sleeping width plus 4 m), a soft ring edge metres wide marking it on the ground, and the legend lying top x radius north of the middle (the circle's far side from the camera), the open floor in front. Quest sigils and relics take effect inside it.

legendClearing.minFromStone.what: its edge at least this many metres from its area's runestone (where the soundsystem comes), clear of the stone's clearing and the party's dance space; a small area with no such spot takes the farthest that fits (logged).

decisions.quote: The legend circle shouldn't spawn near its runestone

legendClearing.minFromOtherStones.what: its edge at least this many metres from every neighbouring area's runestone too, always (not relaxed for a small area).

decisions.quote: Legend and runestone in the same place

legendClearing.floor.what: on, old flagstones about slab metres across, the legend's sigil carved into them as dark grooves, overgrowth (0.5 as drawn, up to 1 for more) moss, grass and litter over them so the carving shows only in pieces.

decisions.quote: The floor of the legend circle can be weathered and mossy stone with the legend's sigil carved into it. It's covered by moss etc and so you can't see it clearly

legendClearing.floor.glint.what: how much the grooves catch the light while its legend sleeps (0, off: Ed's call later).

legendClearing.rim.what: art builder 3's rim kit (#262) round its edge, a piece every spacing metres of it at chance, out metres past its radius and up to spread more (on its ring, never its floor), none on a path nor within gap degrees of due south [1].

decisions.quote: legend circles should always be hidden by scenery around them
decisions.rest: 0 since:: the stones go all the way round

legendClearing.grove.what: The forest swells thicker and taller round the edge of a legend's clearing.

decisions.quote: an area of the tallest trees around each legend circle
It should blend back smoothly into the rest of the forest around this area, so it doesn't stand out too much
legend circles should always be hidden by scenery around them
decisions.rest: both 0 since:: the ring of trees goes all the way round, the circle hidden until she walks in, her see-through hole showing it then

legendClearing.grove.notes: round the circle's ragged edge the forest swells, strongest at the edge and easing out (smoothstep) over reach metres to the area's own: there trees stand at up to density (a chance a tree spot), up to tallest of them the area's two tallest kinds, drawn up to scale times bigger, each tree's strength jittered by jitter either way so no ring or step shows; open in front gap degrees either side of due south (toward the camera), easing in over soft degrees more [3].

legendClearing.fit.what: Each legend's clearing is sized to its legend as drawn asleep, with a margin to spare.

decisions.quote: Legend circles need to be larger. Often legends don't fit in them

legendClearing.fit.notes: each circle sized to its legend as drawn asleep (config/legend-footprints.json, measured by node tools/legends/footprint.mjs), its sleeping body fitting where it lies with margin metres to spare, never smaller than species (or radius) gives it, never more than max metres (past about 25 a circle can't be placed in its area clear of the runestones); in a legend area of its own (legends.areas) at most areaMax metres, at the area's heart, clear of the runestones round it by minFromOtherStones.

relics.what: Modern relics (cars, trolleys, cones, highway slabs, a phone box, a sofa) scattered through the forest, more of them near roads.
relics.notes: Modern relics (cars, trolleys, cones, highway slabs, a phone box, a sofa...): one chance per spacing-metre cell (chance, steered by the area's decor share of modern), nearRoad times as likely within 20 m of a road or railway; never on a path, in a central clearing or a ground; at least minGap metres from the next relic (Ed, v147: too numerous).

walls.what: Garden walls, hedges, brambles and rock walls running through the areas, along paths where there are some.
walls.notes: Wall objects as features (Ed, v147), per area: man-made and linear ones (garden walls, hedges, brambles, rock walls) as runs [min,max] of runLength [min,max] pieces joined end to end, along a path where one passes (with a gateway gap gateChance of the time; a garden's flower beds in a row along them); henge stones as rings [min,max] of ringStones [min,max] (the first round the shrine, others ringRadius [min,max] metres across in a glade), an avenue leading in avenueChance of the time, and a lone stone loneChance; water, reeds and boulders as clumps [min,max] of clumpSize [min,max] within clumpRadius metres. Open ground between.

decor.what: Ruins, rocks and freak trees scattered as discoveries, fewer under dense canopy.
decor.notes: Decorations scattered as discoveries: one chance per spacing-metre cell, of a ruin (ruins), a rock (rocks) or a freak tree (freak), each at least minGap metres from the next (Ed, v147: too numerous); fewer under dense canopy; never in an area's central clearing (openness under clearing), on or within pathGap metres of a path, or by the dancefloor.

decor.mix.what: each family's share times its factor, 1 as each area authors it [1].

decisions.rest: ruins twice as many, about 6 an island, which with the island taking its finds first is 1.5; no rocks, no freak trees

decor.footprint.what: metres round a decoration kept clear of soundsystems, the dancefloor, the treehouse and set pieces (plus reserveMargin).

paths.what: Railways, old roads and streams crossing the island.

decisions.quote: There are much too many paths
decisions.rest: linkChance 0.55 to 0.1, deadEndChance 0.3 to 0, rails [2,4] to [0,1], at most one railway

paths.notes: Paths, roads and railways (Ed): far fewer since 2026-10-11 [1]. rails [min,max] railway lines edge to edge in wide curves (one with a branch); roads [min,max] broad sweeping old roads (0: Ed, round 13, "remove the paths that are roads: only the kind that cars might drive on"; footpaths, railways and streams stay).

paths.linkChance.what: the share of neighbouring areas joined by a meandering path.

paths.deadEndChance.what: the share of areas with a path out to nothing.

paths.pathHalf.what: How wide the paths are kept clear of trees, with thick bushes along their edges.
paths.pathHalf.notes: half each corridor's width (metres), kept clear of trees, with bushes thick along the edges for edgeBushes metres (bushBoost times as many); streams [min,max] long streams winding across the map (and short ones join wet areas that touch), streamHalf metres half-wide; along a railway, every landmarkSpacing metres, a landmarkChance of a landmark (a wagon, a carriage, a platform, a gantry) and otherwise sometimes a signal post; verge posts along roads every vergeSpacing metres; every 3D piece at least pieceGap metres from the next.

paths.railBroken.what: the share of the railway that's broken, where trees grow between the sleepers (treesOnBroken times the usual chance).

paths.pieces.what: false places none of these 3D pieces at all [1].

decisions.rest: the small islands: no landmarks, signals, buffer stops, stairs, bridges or fingerposts; paths cross streams without a bridge

paths.fingerposts.what: a fingerpost by each footpath where it comes into a clearing (the prop generator's; the game turns it on: app/linkParams.ts); the two flights of stairs are finds, each at most once per map, by the clearing of a ravine, rocky slope, cave mouth or stone shrine.

setPieceChance.what: the share of areas, among the types that have a set piece, that show theirs. Wall objects are laid out as features (see walls); they do not block movement. [1]

setPieceFootprint.what: Scenery keeps clear of the gameplay places: soundsystems, legends and the like.
setPieceFootprint.notes: Gameplay is placed first, then scenery keeps clear of it: a set piece's footprint (setPieceFootprint metres round its middle, times setPieceScale) stays reserveMargin metres clear of every soundsystem's spot (soundsystemFootprint metres round it, reserved from the start) and of the dancefloor's clearing; a set piece with no room left is left out. Trees keep treeMarginFromSoundsystem metres from a soundsystem's footprint.

stoneKeepClear.what: The keep-clear zone round each area's stone (its great stump, or its runestone with the stumps off), in metres from its middle.
stoneKeepClear.notes: Nothing special within it: no scene or set piece, ruin or freak tree (the giant mushroom), modern relic, the night's find, flask (party relic), legend's clearing, wall or stone ring, pond, campfire or magic stone, the party's picnics, clusters, set dressing and campfires, or ground (playgrounds and sports grounds): each keeps its whole footprint out (clearOfStones in rules/map.ts). Ordinary trees, bushes, rocks and groundcover may stand in it; the stump's own clearing (runeMarkers.stump.clear) keeps the trees off its roots. A legend's clearing that can't fit out of it (a small area) goes at the farthest spot it fits, and the map says so in the log. The 40 m: the stump's 17 m clearing and a margin.

decisions.quote: No special areas should appear so close to stump/runestone areas; no special scenery, no finds or flasks, no legend circles
decisions.rest: and the party relics, walls and ruins, ponds, picnics and campfires, and the playgrounds too
